title: Bomb calorimeter — how does it work?

A.title: How a bomb calorimeter measures heat

caption.hook: How does a bomb calorimeter measure the heat of a reaction? 🔥
caption.body: A sample burns inside a sealed steel bomb, the heat flows into the water, and the thermometer gives the temperature rise, ΔT. The calorimeter's known heat capacity turns that into the heat released: q_V = −C ΔT. Filmed in the real PrayogX 3-D simulation.

B.title: Why a bomb calorimeter measures ΔU

caption.hook: Why does a bomb calorimeter measure ΔU? ⚗️
caption.body: The bomb's rigid steel walls keep the volume constant, so the gases cannot do expansion work: w = 0. The first law, ΔU = q + w, then gives ΔU = q_V = −C ΔT. Filmed in the real PrayogX 3-D simulation.
